description: Turns a phasor into a Euclidean rhythm set by steps, fill and rotation, with gates on the filled steps, a clock on every step and a ramp across each Euclidean beat

params.text: Sets how many steps the pattern has, 1 to 64, 16 when new
Attenuverts the steps CV, -1 to +1; at full depth 5V adds 64 steps
Sets how many steps are filled, 0 to 64, 4 when new; the filled steps are spread as evenly as the step count allows
Attenuverts the fill CV, -1 to +1; at full depth 5V adds 64 to the fill
Rotates the filled steps through the pattern, a whole turn either way at the extremes
Sets the width of the gate and clock pulses, from no pulse at -5V through 50% at the centre to a gate that never drops at +5V
Attenuverts the pulse width CV, -1 to +1
Picks what happens when fill passes the step count: clamp it, swap fill and steps, wrap it, fold it, ratchet, or read fill as a density across the steps
Nothing in the module reads this control; the fill mode CV is scaled by the fill attenuverter instead
Free lets the step count take fractional values; Quant. holds steps and rotation to whole numbers
Free lets fill take fractional values; Quant. holds fill to whole numbers
Instant applies knob and CV changes at once; the other position holds a change back until the next step begins
Raw compares the phasor against the width setting directly; Smart mutes the outputs when the phasor is not moving and mirrors the pulses when it runs backwards

inputs.text: The phasor read as the pattern, 0-10V
Adds to the step count, scaled by the steps attenuverter
Adds to the fill, scaled by the fill attenuverter
Adds to the rotation, scaled by the rotation attenuverter
Adds to the pulse width, scaled by the pulse width attenuverter
Adds to the fill limit mode selection, scaled by the fill attenuverter

outputs.text: A 0-10V ramp across the current Euclidean beat, so a long gap between filled steps gives a long ramp
A 10V gate on each filled step of the pattern
A 10V pulse on every step, filled or not

notes: a phasor drives this, not a clock: a ramp rising from 0V to 10V once per cycle, from Phasor Generator, Clock to Phasor or an LFO's saw output. Nothing moves here until one is patched in.
